the_signal.headline: n8n Agents ship: workflow automation enters agentic era
the_signal.body: n8n's new Agents feature lets you describe what you want, pick a model, and route it to tools and workflows—no custom code required. This moves agentic patterns from research into GTM infrastructure. For revenue teams, this means faster deployment of AI-powered lead routing, qualification, and follow-up without waiting for engineering sprints.

tool_drop.name: n8n Agents
tool_drop.what: Declarative agent framework that chains models, tools, and workflows without custom orchestration code.
tool_drop.why: Cuts the gap between 'we want an AI agent' and 'it's routing leads' from months to days—direct GTM velocity play.

thread_of_day.title: Agentic CUDA Kernel Optimizer: agents debugging agents
thread_of_day.takeaway: Someone used LangGraph agents to optimize CUDA kernels by handing them a C++ test harness—shows agents are becoming meta-level problem solvers, not just chatbots.

quote.text: Starting with n8n v2.36, you can now use supported AI models and tool services on select n8n Cloud plans without creating a provider account or generating an API key.

whats_moving.context: n8n Agents + reflection patterns shipping together signal orchestration is now the default execution model, not an edge case.
Transactional outbox pattern gaining traction—GTM workflows need guaranteed event delivery, especially for compliance-heavy revenue ops.
Gateway credits eliminating provider account friction is table stakes; expect competitors to match this UX pattern within weeks.

act_on_this: Map your current lead qualification workflow to an n8n Agent prototype this week—test whether agentic routing beats your deterministic rules engine on conversion rate.

numbers.stat: n8n v2.36 eliminates API key setup friction for model access
numbers.context: One less blocker between 'let's try this model' and 'it's in production'—matters for rapid experimentation cycles in GTM.
